queue.question: both readers gave the same answer to every ambiguity listed under "Shared answers"; read the other way, these requirements mean something else: are those answers meant?

"no or more carrots" can mean: 'zero or more': need is a non-negative count that may be 0, and the rabbit eats exactly need carrots when the stock allows (fits eat(5, 6, 10) -> [11, 4] and eat(4, 8, 9) -> [12, 1]) / 'need or more': need is only a minimum and the rabbit may eat more than need carrots when the stock allows. Which is meant?
"an array" can mean: a Python list / any array-like sequence of two integers (list, tuple, array.array, ...). Which is meant?

"needed or eaten" can mean: eaten: number + min(need, remaining), the carrots actually eaten (fits all four examples) / needed: number + need, regardless of the stock (fits eat(5, 6, 10), eat(4, 8, 9) and eat(1, 10, 10), but contradicts eat(2, 11, 5) -> [7, 0], which would give 13). Which is meant?

"before or after your meals" can mean: after the meal: the count includes the carrots eaten in this meal (fits all four examples) / before the meal: the first element is number alone (contradicts every example, e.g. eat(5, 6, 10) would give 5, not 11). Which is meant?

"total number" can mean: the total includes the carrots eaten before the meal (number) plus those eaten in it (fits all four examples) / only the carrots eaten in this meal, min(need, remaining) (contradicts every example, e.g. eat(5, 6, 10) would give 6, not 11). Which is meant?

"needed or eaten left" can mean: carrots left in stock after the meal: max(remaining - need, 0) (fits all four examples) / carrots still needed after the meal: max(need - remaining, 0) (contradicts eat(5, 6, 10) -> [11, 4], eat(4, 8, 9) -> [12, 1] and eat(2, 11, 5) -> [7, 0], which would give 0, 0 and 6) / carrots eaten in the meal: min(need, remaining) (contradicts every example, e.g. eat(5, 6, 10) would give 6, not 4). Which is meant?
"not enough remaining carrots" can mean: remaining < need / remaining <= need (at remaining == need both readings give the same returned list). Which is meant?

"will still be hungry" can mean: narrative only: the returned list does not report the shortfall, and the second element stays the stock left, 0 / the returned list reports the unmet need need - remaining, e.g. as the second element (contradicts eat(2, 11, 5) -> [7, 0], which would then be [7, 6]). Which is meant?

"[11, 4]" can mean: the second element is the stock left (10 - 6 = 4), as in reading 1 of R-RET-3 / the second element is the carrots still needed (reading 2 of R-RET-3), which would give [11, 0]: the example contradicts that reading. Which is meant?

"[12, 1]" can mean: the second element is the stock left (9 - 8 = 1), as in reading 1 of R-RET-3 / the second element is the carrots still needed (reading 2 of R-RET-3), which would give [12, 0]: the example contradicts that reading. Which is meant?

"[7, 0]" can mean: [total actually eaten, stock left] = [2 + 5, 0], as in reading 1 of R-RET-2 'needed or eaten', of R-RET-3 and of R-HUN-3 / the first element is the total needed (reading 2 of R-RET-2 'needed or eaten'), which would give 13: the example contradicts that reading / the second element is the carrots still needed, the unmet hunger of R-HUN-3 (reading 2 of R-RET-3 and of R-HUN-3), which would give 6: the example contradicts that reading. Which is meant?
